title: nvme-enumeration-scratchpad
content:
Summary:
Observed intermittent node NotReady flaps on scale-up nodes with local NVMe SSDs attached. Pattern: new node boots, cloud-init partitions local SSDs and returns, kubelet starts, and within 30-120s kubelet reports mount failures and NodeNotReady. Suspect race between device enumeration (udev) and kubelet/volume plugin mount attempts.

What I tried (chronological):
- Reproduced by rapidly scaling a batch job that allocates 3 ephemeral-local PVCs on new nodes. Flap reproduced ~30% of attempts.
- Collected logs: kubelet journal, kernel dmesg, cloud-init log, containerd status, /dev/disk/by-id snapshots.
- Useful commands I ran repeatedly:
  - journalctl -u kubelet -o short-precise --no-pager | sed -n '1,250p'  # capture mount errors and node status updates
  - sudo dmesg --ctime | tail -n 200  # look for nvme registration and timeout messages
  - lsblk -o NAME,MAJ:MIN,SIZE,RO,TYPE,MOUNTPOINT  # confirm devices present
  - ls -l /dev/disk/by-id | grep nvme || true  # check by-id symlink timing
  - sudo udevadm monitor --kernel --udev --subsystem-match=block  # observe real-time device events during attach
  - sudo udevadm settle --timeout=15; ls -l /dev/nvme*; ls -l /dev/disk/by-id/*nvme* || true
  - sudo cat /var/log/cloud-init.log | tail -n 50  # check partition/mkfs completion timestamps
  - systemctl status kubelet containerd --no-pager

Representative log snippets (paraphrased to avoid verbatim long traces):
- kubelet: nestedpendingoperations: operation for "mount" failed: exit status 32; volume_manager: could not mount '/var/lib/kubelet/pods/.../volumes/...': no such file or directory
- kubelet: Failed to update node status: context deadline exceeded
- kernel/dmesg: nvme0n1: registered; later a device timed out on sda on one run; on another run kernel logged rescan and nvme enumerated as nvme2
- cloud-init: partitioning and mkfs completed, then a few seconds later kubelet started (timestamps close)

Hypotheses (ordered):
1) udev enumeration lag: NVMe device nodes appear but by-id symlinks are created a few seconds later; volume plugin tries to mount using by-id and fails quickly without sufficient retries.
2) ordering: kubelet starts before cloud-init's disk prep is fully propagated to udev; we rely on sleep-based waits in cloud-init that are flaky.
3) containerd snapshotter contention: overlayfs snapshot creation returns EBUSY while the block device is still being manipulated (partition/mkfs), making pod create hang and kubelet mark node NotReady.
4) older custom udev rules in our base image cause device name changes or unpredictable symlink targets on certain instance families.

Quick experiments and results:
- Replaced sleep with 'udevadm settle' in cloud-init after mkfs: reduced flaps in small sample (n=10).
- Added 'After=cloud-final.service' to kubelet systemd unit: in a canary pool of 20 nodes saw zero flaps during short soak (but sample small).
- Touching /var/lib/cloud/finished as a crude kubelet delay: helped but not reliable.
- Switching mounts to reference UUIDs avoided by-id timing issues in a single-node test but is awkward for ephemeral local SSD workflow and harder to bake universally.

Troubleshooting checklist for next run (copyable):
- Start watch: watch -n 0.2 "date; systemctl is-active kubelet; ls -l /dev/disk/by-id | grep nvme || true; tail -n 6 /var/log/cloud-init.log"
- In parallel: sudo udevadm monitor --kernel --udev --subsystem-match=block > /tmp/udev-events.log &
- After repro attempt: collect full journals: sudo journalctl -u kubelet --since '5 minutes ago' > /tmp/kubelet-journal.log; sudo dmesg > /tmp/dmesg.log; lsblk -o NAME,MAJ:MIN,SIZE,RO,TYPE,MOUNTPOINT > /tmp/lsblk.txt

Edge observations and oddities:
- On one instance the NVMe disappeared and reappeared with a different index (nvme0 -> nvme2) after a rescan; major:minor changed and by-id symlinks were stale until recreated.
- Spot/interruptible instances show higher flapping rates; likely provider-level detaches and reattaches influence enumeration ordering.
- No evidence of general kubelet resource pressure (no OOM or eviction logs); problem is localized to mount/device timing.

Short-term mitigation plan (practical):
- Bake image change: add 'After=cloud-final.service' and a short ExecStartPre that runs 'udevadm settle --timeout=10' before kubelet starts. Deploy to staging autoscaler pool as canary. (PR exists: infra/commit/7a9c2d4)
- Replace any explicit sleeps in cloud-init disk steps with udevadm settle to make completion deterministic.

Longer-term fixes to consider:
- Tune volume plugin to retry on ENOENT for longer period before giving up, or prefer device UUIDs when available. Evaluate tradeoffs.
- Investigate containerd startup ordering: delay containerd until /var/lib/containerd snapshot dir is stable or instrument overlayfs EBUSY and document.
- Add boot telemetry: record timestamps for cloud-init disk-ready, udev-ready (first NVMe event), kubelet start, and first successful mount. Ship these as structured logs for future incidents.

Notes to pass on to whoever picks this up:
- Start with the watch + udevadm monitor during a scale-up test to capture real-time sequence.
- Focus on device rename patterns and time delta between cloud-init done and by-id being available.
- If you hit an EBUSY in containerd, capture containerd logs and output of 'stat /var/lib/containerd' during the event.

References and tickets:
- JIRA-INFRA-3124 (investigation)
- infra repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/commit/7a9c2d4
- infra slack: #infra-nodeops thread-req-12345
